articles.title: Asos customers receive ‘hack’ notification threatening leak
articles.summary: Push message claims fashion company’s data has been ‘fully compromised’, but website and app remain online. Business live – latest updates. Asos is investigating after users of its mobile app received a notification claiming hackers had “fully compromised” the online fashion retailer’s data.
body: The value of Asos’s shares on the London Stock Exchange dived almost 12% after thousands of customers received a notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link that sent them to the Telegram messaging service.
The website and app appeared to be continuing to operate on Tuesday morning and it is understood that Asos is still investigating whether any hack has taken place.
The message sent out to customers said: “Dear Asos DPO [data protection officer] and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance.”

Snowflake is a cloud platform used to store, process and analyse data including transactions and demographic information such as clothing sizes and body measurements. It also enables push notifications to clients’ phones.

articles.title: What have I learned in my 53 years? That I shouldn’t listen to strangers who accost me in the street | Zoe Williams
articles.summary: I was shocked when a man in a van aimed an ageist insult at me. And I regret to say that my son has been no help at all. I was performing an ordinary and not at all illegal cycling manoeuvre recently when a guy in a white van said: “You’re too old to be that stupid.” It was a critique so…
body: Anyway, I was on the way to meet a friend and, when I described this ageist abuse to him, he said, having quite a theatrical turn of phrase: “Darling, you’re not old enough to be this stupid.”

I should have been mollified by that and put the episode behind me. Instead, I described it to my 17-year-old, who now refers to it like a yardstick any time I do something stupid. What’s the right age at which to miss a train? How about also missing the return train? If you can’t figure out how to unplug a dishwasher, should you be in your early 30s, or would 41 be correct? Is there a tech inversion by which you can be too young to be that stupid, but no age is too old, given that, the older you are, the more obvious it is that all your unnamable skills were amassed for an era that no longer exists?

Nope, all that notwithstanding, you should still go through life getting better at it. There is no misstep in the world for which 53 is not too old. Apparently, this gets funnier and funnier the more situations to which it is applied.
The wisdom I should have acquired across these acres of time? When someone says a mean thing and you don’t want it to stick, try not telling anyone.

And I regret to say that my son has been no help at all.

articles.title: Chanel is all about joy as Blazy celebrates year at helm of world’s hottest brand
articles.summary: Artistic director is all smiles as he swaps quiet luxury for bold colours and patterns at Paris show. “It’s a good start,” Matthieu Blazy said after a Paris show that marked a year of his tenure as artistic director at Chanel.
body: Chanel now holds the top spot in the Lyst index of the world’s hottest brands, which tracks demand and engagement across search and social media. The privately held company announces official financial results only once a year, but figures reported by Bloomberg showed 16% growth in the first half of 2026. In Vanity Fair’s list of the world’s 50 most powerful people, published this month, Blazy is the only fashion designer to make the cut. People who don’t much care about fashion have noticed him; people who do care about fashion talk about him non-stop.

Blazy’s Chanel is about joy. Smiley and chatty in person, he enthuses about his team and the women he dresses, presenting a friendly face of Chanel that contrasts with Karl Lagerfeld’s legendary acid tongue and Coco’s controlled brutalist chic. He talks about his job like a child in a candy store, not a tortured artist: he got the idea for this stage set, a flock of 95 giant white birds suspended from the domed steel and glass ceiling of the Grand Palais in Paris, while on holiday in southern Italy with his partner, watching migrating birds fly above the Crati River.

articles.title: Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over ‘deceptively similar’ four-stripe clothing
articles.summary: Sports clothing brand bought allegedly trademark-contravening clothes and copies of ubiquitous White Fox bus ads to present in court. Adidas has sued White Fox Boutique over its omnipresent advertisements and sales of clothes with four stripes, alleging breach of its three-stripe trademark.
body: The German-headquartered sports clothing brand accused White Fox of rejecting its repeated requests to stop selling the clothes in filings in the federal court of Australia.
Adidas said its representatives then bought a dozen of the contravening items and photographed their ubiquitous ads on Sydney’s bus network, presented as proof to the court.
White Fox’s social media shows it began selling products with four stripes in January 2026.
Adidas said the clothes were “substantially identical with or otherwise deceptively similar” to its own trademark products, in claims first filed in September and updated on Thursday.

articles.title: How Rachel Ojuromi, the Coolest Girl in Nigeria, Came to Walk the Chanel Show
articles.summary: 22-year-old Rachel Ojuromi turned Lagos into her runway with her viral outfit videos. Then Chanel came calling for the spring 2027 show in Paris.
body: She has rightly been making the most of it. By her second night in the city, Ojuromi had gathered her friends for a 3 a.m. pilgrimage to the Eiffel Tower, calling others back home in Nigeria to share the moment. And she’s been back again. “I really, really love looking at the Eiffel Tower,” she says, laughing. There have been chicken and fries (“the French fries are actually really good”), long conversations with friends, and matcha runs. But nothing quite compares to what came next. Last night, Rachel Ojuromi made her runway debut at Chanel.

Lagos remains fundamental to the way Ojuromi sees herself. Born and raised in Nigeria, she has spoken about the city as something embedded in everything she makes; even as those street-side walks began travelling far beyond it, they remained unmistakably rooted there. In Paris, that instinct suddenly found itself transported onto fashion’s most rarefied stage.

articles.title: Victoria Beckham Is Breaking One Very British Lipstick Rule
articles.summary: Budgeproof, smudge-proof, and transfer-proof, housed in a luxurious white case, the new Rogue Victoria red lipstick collection is designed to make wearing red lipstick effortless.
body: If there’s one lesson from finishing school that’s stayed with Victoria Beckham all these years, it’s that “a lady should never touch up her lipstick at the dinner table.” “I really questioned why,” Beckham says of the edict decreed by one of her mother’s friends, “because I think there’s something very ceremonial about reapplying your lipstick.”

Lipstick, then, wasn’t just about wearing it—but the art of applying it. Throughout her life and career, Beckham seems to have maintained a level of polish with her glam—marked by soft, natural skin, an eye look smoked out to perfection, and a lip with posh-level precision, all things that make her makeup looks so enviable.

More often than not, you’ll find the superstar in a pinkish nude—the inspiration behind her Posh Lipstick collection which debuted in 2020. Back then, she wanted to perfect the nude lip through a range of creamy, nourishing pigments; six years later, she’s set out to do the same for the sensual red.

From venture capital investments and startup launches to product drops and regulatory updates, we’ll make sure you never miss a beat when it comes to the AI news that matters.
The news: Trump orders the US government to stop calling AI “AI”.

Why it matters: President Donald Trump has signed an executive order instructing the US government to replace “artificial intelligence” and “AI” with “super intelligence” and “SI” across all official communications and policy documents, arguing that the new terminology better reflects the tech’s rapidly advancing capabilities and economic potential. articles.title: Why Is Big Tech Trying to Make AI Agents the New Labubus?
articles.summary: Meta and OpenAI have rolled out fuzzy, kawaii-coded personal agents to handle everything from emails to shopping. But experts warn that users, brands and the internet itself aren’t equipped to manage the risks.
body: In the last two weeks, Meta released its personal AI assistant, Muse, while OpenAI released its Dots AI agent. The promise is that these agents can autonomously act on users’ behalves, from answering emails and sending invoices to booking flights and buying clothes. What’s notable is their kawaii-coded wrapping: unnervingly advanced bots dressed up as cute, unthreatening companions. OpenAI’s Dots are puffy rainbow colored blobs donning sunglasses and berets. Meta’s Muse agent mascot, named Jolly, is a fuzzy, chubby, rosy-cheeked creature that’s part-Labubu, part-Squishmallow.

It will soon come with the Muse Charm, a Tamagotchi-like accessory bearing the mascot’s face that can be activated by a fingerprint sensor. “We’ve packed a lot of technology for this little guy to fit onto a keychain and always be available to talk to,” Mark Zuckerberg said in his keynote at the annual Meta Connect conference in September. Meta is yet to confirm whether the Muse Charm will feature cameras and microphones, but Zuckerberg added on stage: “You just go ahead and tap here in the fingerprint sensor in the corner and you can start talking.”
points: Meta and OpenAI have rolled out fuzzy, kawaii-coded personal agents to handle everything from emails to shopping.
But experts warn that users, brands and the internet itself aren’t equipped to manage the risks.

articles.title: The Farmers Market Is Built for Solo Cooking
articles.summary: I can buy a single carrot, radish, and cucumber without batting an eye.
body: Most recipes serve multiple people. In Me, Myself, and Dinner, each dish serves one and only one. That's you! Because whether you live solo (almost 30% of Americans do) or are enjoying a night to yourself, sitting down to a meal should be something to look forward to.

Everyone romanticizes the summer farmers market. And yes, there’s nothing more beautiful on God’s green earth than taking a bite out of a ripe beefsteak tomato like a juicy apple. But fall has its own kind of magic. Giant gooseneck gourds, Honeycrisps dripping with nectar, bunches of full, frilly kale. When presented with that kind of abundance, how can you impose self-restraint?

Good news is you don’t have to. Farmers markets are built for exactly this kind of behavior. The produce is sold loose, meaning you can buy one of anything that catches your eye. And when I’m cooking solo, that’s the ultimate cheat code. I don’t need to commit to a giant bag of carrots. Instead, I can buy a single iridescent peachy-pink carrot, because how fun?
